strings.hub.symbols.title: Sacred Symbols
strings.hub.symbols.subtitle: The signs of the faith
strings.hub.symbols.intro: A cross on a spire, a fish scratched on a wall, four winged creatures around a Gospel book. The Catholic Church speaks in signs. Here is what they mean.
strings.sec.symbols.crosses.title: The Cross & Its Forms
strings.sec.symbols.crosses.summary: The central sign of the faith, and the many crosses that grew from it.
strings.art.symbols.crosses.title: The Cross & Its Forms
strings.art.symbols.crosses.lead: Every one of these is a variation on a single sign: Christ's victory through the Cross.
strings.sym.cross.name: The Cross
strings.sym.cross.desc: The near-universal sign of the Catholic faith — Christ's saving death and his victory over it — found on churches, altars, homes and graves.
strings.sym.crucifix.name: The Crucifix
strings.sym.crucifix.desc: A cross bearing the figure of the crucified Christ, keeping his sacrifice before the eyes of the faithful — above altars, in homes, and on the rosary.
strings.sym.inri.name: INRI
strings.sym.inri.desc: The Latin initials for “Jesus of Nazareth, King of the Jews,” the charge Pilate fixed above the Cross, still lettered on crucifixes.
strings.sym.papal_cross.name: The Papal Cross
strings.sym.papal_cross.desc: A cross with three descending bars, reserved to the Pope, appearing in heraldry and on ceremonial occasions.
strings.sym.jerusalem_cross.name: The Jerusalem Cross
strings.sym.jerusalem_cross.desc: A large cross ringed by four smaller ones — Christ and the spread of the Gospel to the four corners of the earth; a badge of the Holy Land and of pilgrims.
strings.sym.maltese_cross.name: The Maltese Cross
strings.sym.maltese_cross.desc: An eight-pointed cross of Christian service and sacrifice, worn by the Order of Malta and taken up by many Catholic charities.
strings.sym.tau_cross.name: The Tau Cross
strings.sym.tau_cross.desc: A cross shaped like the Greek letter T — a biblical sign of protection (Ezekiel 9) especially loved by St Francis and the Franciscans.
strings.sym.st_andrew_cross.name: St Andrew's Cross
strings.sym.st_andrew_cross.desc: An X-shaped cross, the form on which the apostle Andrew was said to be martyred, and now his attribute.
strings.sym.christ_king.name: Cross, Crown & Orb
strings.sym.christ_king.desc: Christ the King shown with crown, cross and orb, ruling over all creation.
strings.sec.symbols.holy_name.title: The Holy Name & Christograms
strings.sec.symbols.holy_name.summary: Monograms and letters that stand in for the name of Christ himself.
strings.art.symbols.holy_name.title: The Holy Name & Christograms
strings.art.symbols.holy_name.lead: Long before printed words, these letter-signs named Christ in stone and gold.
strings.sym.chi_rho.name: Chi-Rho (☩)
strings.sym.chi_rho.desc: The first two Greek letters of Christos (Χ and Ρ) laid over each other — Constantine's labarum, still used on altars, vestments and sacred art.
strings.sym.chi_rho_alpha_omega.name: Chi-Rho with Alpha & Omega
strings.sym.chi_rho_alpha_omega.desc: The Chi-Rho flanked by Alpha and Omega — Christ's name joined to “the beginning and the end,” a favourite on Paschal candles and in early Christian art.
strings.sym.ihs.name: IHS / IHC
strings.sym.ihs.desc: A monogram of the Holy Name from the first letters of Jesus in Greek; also read as Iesus Hominum Salvator. Marks hosts, altars and Jesuit emblems.
strings.sym.alpha_omega.name: Alpha & Omega (Α Ω)
strings.sym.alpha_omega.desc: The first and last letters of the Greek alphabet — Christ as the beginning and the end (Revelation), lettered on Paschal candles, churches and tombs.
strings.sym.ichthys.name: The Fish (Ichthys)
strings.sym.ichthys.desc: An early secret sign for Christ: the Greek word for fish, ICHTHYS, spells an acrostic for “Jesus Christ, God's Son, Saviour.”
strings.sym.labarum.name: XP with Wreath
strings.sym.labarum.desc: The Chi-Rho set within a victor's wreath, an early sign of the triumph of Christ over death.
strings.sec.symbols.christ.title: Christ the Redeemer
strings.sec.symbols.christ.summary: Images of Christ as Lamb, Shepherd and Sacred Heart.
strings.art.symbols.christ.title: Christ the Redeemer
strings.art.symbols.christ.lead: These images show who Christ is and what his love has done.
strings.sym.agnus_dei.name: Agnus Dei / Lamb of God
strings.sym.agnus_dei.desc: Christ as the sacrificial Lamb, often shown standing with the banner of the Resurrection — on altars, tabernacles and stained glass.
strings.sym.good_shepherd.name: The Good Shepherd
strings.sym.good_shepherd.desc: Christ carrying the lost sheep on his shoulders, one of the oldest Christian images of his care for his people.
strings.sym.sacred_heart.name: The Sacred Heart
strings.sym.sacred_heart.desc: The heart of Jesus crowned with thorns and aflame — his divine love and mercy for humanity, a central modern devotion.
strings.sym.crown_of_thorns.name: The Crown of Thorns
strings.sym.crown_of_thorns.desc: The thorns pressed on Christ at his Passion, a sign of his mockery and suffering.
strings.sym.five_wounds.name: The Five Wounds
strings.sym.five_wounds.desc: The wounds in Christ's hands, feet and side, honoured in devotion and heraldry.
strings.sym.pelican.name: Pelican in Her Piety
strings.sym.pelican.desc: A pelican feeding its young with its own blood — a medieval emblem of Christ nourishing humanity in the Eucharist, carved on tabernacles.
strings.sym.pantocrator.name: Christ Pantocrator
strings.sym.pantocrator.desc: Christ as ruler and judge of all, blessing with one hand and holding the book — set in domes and apses since the early Church.
strings.sec.symbols.evangelists.title: The Four Evangelists
strings.sec.symbols.evangelists.summary: The tetramorph: the winged creatures that stand for Matthew, Mark, Luke and John.
strings.art.symbols.evangelists.title: The Four Evangelists
strings.art.symbols.evangelists.lead: From Ezekiel and Revelation, four living creatures became the sign of the four Gospels.
strings.sym.tetramorph.name: The Tetramorph
strings.sym.tetramorph.desc: The four living creatures gathered as one emblem — winged man, lion, ox and eagle — the four Gospels together, set around Christ or a Gospel book on ambos, mosaics and church façades.
strings.sym.evangelist_matthew.name: Winged Man — Matthew
strings.sym.evangelist_matthew.desc: The winged man (or angel) stands for Matthew, whose Gospel opens with the human ancestry of Christ.
strings.sym.evangelist_mark.name: Winged Lion — Mark
strings.sym.evangelist_mark.desc: The winged lion stands for Mark, whose Gospel begins with a voice crying in the wilderness.
strings.sym.evangelist_luke.name: Winged Ox — Luke
strings.sym.evangelist_luke.desc: The winged ox stands for Luke, whose Gospel opens in the Temple with the sacrifice of Zechariah.
strings.sym.evangelist_john.name: Eagle — John
strings.sym.evangelist_john.desc: The eagle stands for John, whose Gospel soars from its first words into the mystery of the Word made flesh.
strings.sec.symbols.spirit_trinity.title: The Holy Spirit & the Trinity
strings.sec.symbols.spirit_trinity.summary: The dove, the fire, and the ways art points to the Three in One.
strings.art.symbols.spirit_trinity.title: The Holy Spirit & the Trinity
strings.art.symbols.spirit_trinity.lead: How do you picture God who is one and three? These are the Church's answers.
strings.sym.dove.name: The Dove
strings.sym.dove.desc: The Holy Spirit, descending in a shaft of light — seen in art of the Baptism, Confirmation and Pentecost.
strings.sym.tongues_of_fire.name: Tongues of Fire
strings.sym.tongues_of_fire.desc: The flames that rested on the apostles at Pentecost, a sign of the Spirit poured out; common in Confirmation imagery.
strings.sym.seven_flames.name: Seven Flames
strings.sym.seven_flames.desc: Seven small flames for the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit, often shown around a dove or a confirmand.
strings.sym.triangle.name: The Triangle
strings.sym.triangle.desc: Three equal sides for the one God in three Persons — a simple emblem of the Holy Trinity.
strings.sym.all_seeing_eye.name: Eye in the Triangle
strings.sym.all_seeing_eye.desc: The eye of God within a radiant triangle, an older sign of divine Providence watching over all.
strings.sym.three_circles.name: Three Interlocking Circles
strings.sym.three_circles.desc: Three rings joined as one, each equal and inseparable — the unity of the Trinity.
strings.sym.trefoil.name: The Trefoil
strings.sym.trefoil.desc: A three-lobed form, at once a leaf and a sign of the Three-in-One, worked into Gothic tracery.
strings.sym.hand_of_god.name: The Hand of God
strings.sym.hand_of_god.desc: A hand reaching from a cloud, the Father's action and blessing, common in ancient and Romanesque art.
strings.sec.symbols.eucharist_sacraments.title: The Eucharist & the Sacraments
strings.sec.symbols.eucharist_sacraments.summary: Bread and wine, water and oil, candle and ring — the signs of the sacraments.
strings.art.symbols.eucharist_sacraments.title: The Eucharist & the Sacraments
strings.art.symbols.eucharist_sacraments.lead: The sacraments are visible signs of invisible grace, and each carries its own emblem.
strings.sym.chalice_host.name: Chalice & Host
strings.sym.chalice_host.desc: The cup and the bread of the Eucharist, the Body and Blood of Christ — the heart of Catholic worship and of First Communion imagery.
strings.sym.wheat_grapes.name: Wheat & Grapes
strings.sym.wheat_grapes.desc: Sheaves of wheat and clusters of grapes for the bread and wine of the Mass, carved on chalices and altars.
strings.sym.monstrance.name: The Monstrance
strings.sym.monstrance.desc: A radiant vessel that displays the consecrated Host for adoration, its golden rays a sign of Christ's light.
strings.sym.vine_branches.name: Vine & Branches
strings.sym.vine_branches.desc: “I am the vine, you are the branches” (John 15) — Christ and the Church joined as one living plant.
strings.sym.bread_fish.name: Bread & Fish
strings.sym.bread_fish.desc: The loaves and fishes of the multiplication miracle, an early Eucharistic sign in catacomb art.
strings.sym.candle.name: Candle & Flame
strings.sym.candle.desc: A burning candle for Christ the Light and for the faith kindled at Baptism, present at Baptisms, Easter and funerals.
strings.sym.paschal_candle.name: The Paschal Candle
strings.sym.paschal_candle.desc: The great Easter candle, marked with a cross, Alpha and Omega, and the year — the Risen Christ among his people.
strings.sym.thurible.name: Incense & Thurible
strings.sym.thurible.desc: Rising incense smoke for the prayers of the faithful ascending to God, swung from the thurible at solemn liturgies.
strings.sym.baptismal_shell.name: Shell Pouring Water
strings.sym.baptismal_shell.desc: A shell used to pour the water of Baptism, and a sign of the sacrament itself on fonts and baptisteries.
strings.sym.holy_oils.name: Vessel of Holy Oil
strings.sym.holy_oils.desc: The oils of anointing used at Confirmation, Holy Orders and the Anointing of the Sick.
strings.sym.wedding_rings.name: Wedding Rings
strings.sym.wedding_rings.desc: Two joined rings for the sacrament of Matrimony and the lasting bond of husband and wife.
strings.sym.laying_on_hands.name: Laying On of Hands
strings.sym.laying_on_hands.desc: Hands imposed on the head, the ancient gesture of ordination and of the gift of the Spirit in Confirmation.
strings.sec.symbols.pope_bishops.title: Peter, the Pope & the Bishops
strings.sec.symbols.pope_bishops.summary: The keys, the mitre, the crozier and the other signs of pastoral office.
strings.art.symbols.pope_bishops.title: Peter, the Pope & the Bishops
strings.art.symbols.pope_bishops.lead: The shepherds of the Church carry signs of the authority entrusted to them.
strings.sym.keys_of_peter.name: The Keys of St Peter
strings.sym.keys_of_peter.desc: The gold and silver crossed keys — the authority to bind and loose given to Peter (Matthew 16), the emblem of the papacy and the Holy See.
strings.sym.papal_tiara.name: The Papal Tiara
strings.sym.papal_tiara.desc: The historic triple crown of the popes; no longer worn in the liturgy, it survives on the arms of the Holy See.
strings.sym.ferula.name: The Papal Ferula
strings.sym.ferula.desc: The pastoral staff carried by the Pope, a form of crozier marking his office as shepherd of the whole Church.
strings.sym.pallium.name: The Pallium
strings.sym.pallium.desc: A narrow woollen band worn over the shoulders by the Pope and metropolitan archbishops, a sign of communion with the See of Peter.
strings.sym.mitre.name: The Mitre
strings.sym.mitre.desc: The pointed liturgical headdress of bishops, archbishops and the Pope, a sign of the fullness of Holy Orders.
strings.sym.crozier.name: The Crozier
strings.sym.crozier.desc: The shepherd's crook carried by bishops and abbots, marking their duty to guard and guide the flock.
strings.sym.cathedra.name: The Cathedra
strings.sym.cathedra.desc: The bishop's chair, sign of his teaching authority; the church that holds it is called a cathedral.
strings.sym.pectoral_cross.name: The Pectoral Cross
strings.sym.pectoral_cross.desc: A cross worn on the breast by bishops and cardinals, a sign of their episcopal ministry.
strings.sym.episcopal_ring.name: The Episcopal Ring
strings.sym.episcopal_ring.desc: The ring of a bishop, a sign of his fidelity and his bond to the Church he serves.
strings.sym.barque_of_peter.name: Ship / Barque of Peter
strings.sym.barque_of_peter.desc: The Church shown as a ship riding the storms of history, with Peter at the helm.
strings.sym.rock.name: The Rock
strings.sym.rock.desc: “You are Peter, and on this rock I will build my Church” — a sign of Peter and the stability of the faith.
strings.sec.symbols.scripture_apostles.title: Scripture & the Apostles
strings.sec.symbols.scripture_apostles.summary: The book, the scroll, the sword and the anchor of the apostolic age.
strings.art.symbols.scripture_apostles.title: Scripture & the Apostles
strings.art.symbols.scripture_apostles.lead: The Word of God and those who carried it are remembered by these signs.
strings.sym.gospel_book.name: Open Bible / Gospel Book
strings.sym.gospel_book.desc: The open book of the Word of God, carried in procession and enthroned at councils and ordinations.
strings.sym.seven_seals.name: Book with Seven Seals
strings.sym.seven_seals.desc: The sealed scroll of the Book of Revelation, opened by the Lamb — Christ unveiling the plan of God.
strings.sym.scroll.name: The Scroll
strings.sym.scroll.desc: The rolled book of prophecy and revelation, an attribute of the prophets and apostles.
strings.sym.sword.name: The Sword
strings.sym.sword.desc: The Word of God “sharper than any sword,” and a sign of martyrdom — above all the attribute of St Paul.
strings.sym.net_boat.name: Net & Fishing Boat
strings.sym.net_boat.desc: The nets and boat of the first apostles, called to become “fishers of men.”
strings.sym.anchor.name: The Anchor
strings.sym.anchor.desc: Hope as “an anchor of the soul, sure and firm” (Hebrews 6) — a favourite sign in the catacombs and in funerary art.
strings.sym.seven_branched_lamp.name: The Seven-Branched Lampstand
strings.sym.seven_branched_lamp.desc: The menorah of the Temple, taken up as a sign of the Church's roots in Israel and of the seven spirits before God's throne in the Book of Revelation.
strings.sec.symbols.our_lady.title: Our Lady
strings.sec.symbols.our_lady.summary: The monogram, the lily, the stars and the other emblems of the Virgin Mary.
strings.art.symbols.our_lady.title: Our Lady
strings.art.symbols.our_lady.lead: The Church's art surrounds Mary with a language of flowers, stars and light.
strings.sym.immaculate_heart.name: The Immaculate Heart of Mary
strings.sym.immaculate_heart.desc: Mary's heart, often pierced by a sword and wreathed in roses — her love, her sorrow and her purity.
strings.sym.marian_monogram.name: The Marian Monogram (M / AM)
strings.sym.marian_monogram.desc: The letter M, or the joined letters of Ave Maria, standing for the Virgin on medals, vestments and churches.
strings.sym.fleur_de_lis.name: Fleur-de-lis & Lily
strings.sym.fleur_de_lis.desc: The white lily of purity, an emblem of Mary — and, in another setting, of St Joseph.
strings.sym.rose.name: The Rose
strings.sym.rose.desc: The rose of Mary, the “mystical rose,” and the flower woven through the prayers of the rosary.
strings.sym.twelve_stars.name: The Twelve Stars
strings.sym.twelve_stars.desc: The crown of stars of the Woman of Revelation, read of Mary and of the tribes and apostles.
strings.sym.crescent_moon.name: Moon Beneath Mary's Feet
strings.sym.crescent_moon.desc: The crescent moon on which Mary stands as the Woman of Revelation, central to Immaculate Conception imagery.
strings.sym.serpent.name: Serpent Beneath Her Feet
strings.sym.serpent.desc: The serpent crushed under Mary's heel, her share in Christ's triumph over sin and evil.
strings.sym.miraculous_medal.name: The Miraculous Medal
strings.sym.miraculous_medal.desc: The medal of the Immaculate Conception given to St Catherine Labouré, Mary with rays streaming from her hands.
strings.sym.rosary.name: The Rosary
strings.sym.rosary.desc: The beads of the Marian prayer, contemplating the mysteries of Christ through the eyes of his Mother.
strings.sec.symbols.saints.title: Saints & the Faithful
strings.sec.symbols.saints.summary: The halo, the palm, the crown and the attributes that name a saint.
strings.art.symbols.saints.title: Saints & the Faithful
strings.art.symbols.saints.lead: In sacred art a saint is known by the sign they carry.
strings.sym.halo.name: The Halo / Nimbus
strings.sym.halo.desc: The ring or disc of light around the head of a holy figure, marking sanctity — for saints, angels, Mary and Christ.
strings.sym.cruciform_halo.name: The Cruciform Halo
strings.sym.cruciform_halo.desc: A halo bearing a cross, used only for Christ, distinguishing him among the saints.
strings.sym.palm.name: The Palm Branch
strings.sym.palm.desc: The palm of martyrdom and victory, held by saints who died for the faith.
strings.sym.crown.name: The Crown
strings.sym.crown.desc: The crown of victory and sanctity, given to martyrs and to holy kings and queens.
strings.sym.scallop_shell.name: The Scallop Shell
strings.sym.scallop_shell.desc: The shell of St James and of pilgrimage, and an old sign of Baptism.
strings.sym.joseph_lily.name: Lily & Carpenter's Tools
strings.sym.joseph_lily.desc: The flowering lily of St Joseph's purity and the tools of his trade, marking the foster-father of Jesus.
strings.sec.symbols.resurrection.title: Resurrection & Eternal Life
strings.sec.symbols.resurrection.summary: Older symbols of rising and rebirth: the phoenix, the peacock, the tree of life.
strings.art.symbols.resurrection.title: Resurrection & Eternal Life
strings.art.symbols.resurrection.lead: Christian art borrowed images of new life to speak of the Resurrection.
strings.sym.phoenix.name: The Phoenix
strings.sym.phoenix.desc: The bird reborn from its own ashes, an ancient sign of the Resurrection and eternal life.
strings.sym.peacock.name: The Peacock
strings.sym.peacock.desc: The peacock, whose flesh was thought never to decay — immortality, worked into early Christian mosaics.
strings.sym.butterfly.name: The Butterfly
strings.sym.butterfly.desc: The butterfly emerging from the cocoon, a gentle sign of resurrection and transformed life.
strings.sym.pomegranate.name: The Pomegranate
strings.sym.pomegranate.desc: The fruit whose many seeds burst from one skin, a sign of the unity of the Church and of resurrection.
strings.sym.tree_of_life.name: Cedar / Tree of Life
strings.sym.tree_of_life.desc: The evergreen tree of life, a sign of life, of Christ, and of salvation running through Scripture.
strings.sec.symbols.orders.title: Religious Orders
strings.sec.symbols.orders.summary: The emblems of the great families of religious life.
strings.art.symbols.orders.title: Religious Orders
strings.art.symbols.orders.lead: Each order carries a shield or sign that gathers up its spirit.
strings.sym.franciscan_arms.name: The Franciscan Arms
strings.sym.franciscan_arms.desc: The crossed arms of Christ and St Francis before a cross, the emblem of the Franciscan family.
strings.sym.dominican_cross.name: The Dominican Cross
strings.sym.dominican_cross.desc: The black-and-white cross of the Order of Preachers, founded by St Dominic.
strings.sym.carmelite_shield.name: The Carmelite Shield
strings.sym.carmelite_shield.desc: The mountain and stars of Carmel, sign of the Carmelite way of contemplative prayer.
strings.sym.jesuit_ihs.name: The Jesuit IHS Emblem
strings.sym.jesuit_ihs.desc: The IHS of the Holy Name crowned with a cross and rays, the badge of the Society of Jesus.
strings.sym.benedictine_medal.name: The Benedictine Medal
strings.sym.benedictine_medal.desc: The medal and cross of St Benedict, worn for protection and lettered with a prayer against evil.
strings.sym.augustinian_heart.name: The Flaming Heart
strings.sym.augustinian_heart.desc: The burning heart pierced by arrows, emblem of St Augustine and the Augustinians, sign of love set on fire for God.
